chunks: 4915 - And the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"It is not permissible for anyone to be in a state of janabah in this mosque except me, and 'Alī, and Fāṭimah, and al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, and whoever is from my family, for indeed he is from me."

key_terms.أَهْلِي: my family, referring to the Prophet’s household
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque referred to in the hadith
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: 'Alī عليه السلام, named among the exceptions
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ: Fāṭimah عليها السلام, named among the exceptions
key_terms.لَا يَحِلُّ: it is not permissible; indicates a legal prohibition
key_terms.مِنِّي: from me; expressing intimate affiliation and closeness
key_terms.يُجْنِبَ: to be in a state of janabah, major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Who was exempted from the prohibition of being in a state of janabah in the Prophet’s mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith states a specific ruling concerning remaining in a state of janabah in the mosque, while making an exception for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and designated members of his Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام. It also indicates a special nearness and status for his family through the phrase "for indeed he is from me."

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4915 - The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"It is not permissible for anyone to be in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) in this mosque except for Me (sw), Ali (as), Fatimah {s.a}, Hasan (as), Husayn (as), and whoever is from my family (as), for He (as) is part of Me (sw)."
